title: Phrae–Lampang 3-Day Itinerary — Teak Houses & Horse Carts | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day cross-province trip through Phrae and Lampang, Thailand. Start in Phrae's teak-house old town (Khum Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi), drive Highway 103 about an hour to Lampang, ride a horse cart around the old town, and visit Wat Phra That Lampang Luang — with real opening hours and prices.
keywords: Phrae Lampang, Phrae Lampang itinerary, Lampang horse cart, Phrae teak houses, cross-province Thailand trip
h1:
Phrae–Lampang in 3 Days
Teak Houses & Horse Carts
intro: Phrae and Lampang pair up nicely for a back-to-back trip — they're only about 64–70 km apart on Highway 103, roughly an hour's drive. Phrae has the quiet feel of an old teak town, with century-old aristocratic mansions and a pink heritage house. Lampang still has horse carts trotting around its old town, plus Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, a landmark for northerners. We've laid this out as a 3-day, 2-night trip by car, with opening hours and prices we've checked ahead of time.

blocks.html: This route suits anyone who wants to take the north slow, without elbowing through crowds. Phrae is still a town people pass through more than stop in, so it stays calm. Lampang has one thing you won't find anywhere else in Thailand — the horse carts. We start in Phrae because if you fly or take a bus there first and then move up to Lampang, the rhythm flows better.

items: Phrae–Lampang distance — about 64–70 km on Highway 103 (the Phrae–Ngao road), then onto Phahonyothin Road. The drive takes roughly 1 hour.
Recommended transport — your own car or a rental is easiest, since several sights sit outside the town centres, like Wat Phra That Cho Hae and Wat Phra That Lampang Luang.
No car? — vans and buses run between Phrae and Lampang every day, but once you're in town you'll rely on horse carts, songthaews, or motorbike taxis to get around.
Best time to go — Nov–Feb, when the air is cool and you can sightsee all day. The rainy season is still fine for the wooden houses and temples, but bring an umbrella.

blocks.title: Tip on sequencing
blocks.html: If you want to ride a Lampang horse cart during the day, set aside the morning to early afternoon — the cart queue in front of the old provincial hall runs roughly 06:00–16:00. Kad Kong Ta opens only on Saturday and Sunday evenings, so if you want to walk that market, line up your Saturday or Sunday night with the days you're in Lampang.

The first day stays in central Phrae the whole time. The old town is compact — a short walk or drive gets you everywhere. The highlights are the aristocratic mansions and old teak houses, which are still well preserved.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Phrae old town · Khum Chao Luang · century-old teak houses

items.activity: Start at Khum Chao Luang Mueang Phrae
items.note: A two-storey teak mansion in a Thai–European style from the reign of King Rama V, with 72 fretwork doors and windows in total. It was once the residence of Phrae's last ruling lord.

items.activity: Baan Wongburi (Khum Wongburi), the century-old pink house
items.note: A golden-teak house more than 120 years old, with pink gingerbread fretwork. Open 09:00–16:00, admission 30 THB for adults and 15 THB for children. It's a favourite photo spot.

items.activity: Break for lunch — try khanom jeen nam ngiao or khao soi in town
items.note: Phrae has several long-standing khanom jeen nam ngiao shops in the old-town area, with the bold, properly northern flavour.
An applied Thai-style house on a large plot, built with more than a hundred large teak pillars. It clearly shows the prosperity of Phrae's teak-trading era.
The relic temple for those born in the Year of the Tiger, with an octagonal Chiang Saen–style chedi. It's a temple paired with the town of Phrae, about 9 km outside the centre — an easy drive.

items.activity: Have dinner in town and relax
items.note: If you come on a Saturday, look for the old-town market / Phrae walking street to stroll and snack.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Morning in Phrae, Then Drive to Lampang

blocks.html: On the morning of day two, pick up the parts of Phrae you haven't seen yet — especially Baan Thung Hong, the home of mor hom indigo cloth, Phrae's signature craft. Then, from late morning to midday, drive up Highway 103 toward Lampang. You can stop at Wat Phra That Lampang Luang just before reaching the city, which times out nicely.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Phrae mor hom cloth → Highway 103 → Wat Phra That Lampang Luang

items.activity: Baan Thung Hong, the mor hom cloth community
items.note: Phrae's source for indigo-dyed mor hom cloth. There are shops selling clothing, and some houses run tie-dye workshops you can try. It makes a good souvenir to take home.

items.activity: Set off on Highway 103 heading for Lampang
items.note: About 64–70 km, roughly a 1-hour drive. The road is in good shape and easy going.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
items.note: One of the oldest Lanna temples, about 18 km southwest of the city. Open 07:30–17:00. The highlight is the upside-down reflection of the chedi cast inside a darkened hall.

items.activity: Lunch around Ko Kha district, then head into Lampang town
items.note: This area has local restaurants and noodle shops worth a stop, before driving on into town for another 15–20 minutes.

items.activity: Check in to your Lampang accommodation and take a breather
items.note: Pick a place along the Wang River or near Kad Kong Ta so it's easy to walk around at night.

items.activity: Stroll along the Wang River and see Ratchadaphisek Bridge in the evening
items.note: The old white bridge is a symbol of the town and photographs beautifully at sunset.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Horse Carts and Lampang's Old Town

blocks.html: The last day is all about Lampang. The star of the day is the horse cart — Lampang is the only town in Thailand that still has horse carts genuinely carrying tourists. You can ride along enjoying the old town and the antique shophouses on the old market road, then close the trip with chicken-bowl ceramic souvenirs.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Horse cart around town · Kad Kong Ta · chicken-bowl ceramics

items.activity: Catch a horse cart at the queue by the old provincial hall
items.note: Rates from the Lampang Horse Cart Association: 150 THB for a short loop, 200 THB for a longer loop, and 300 THB per hour to charter. The queue runs roughly 06:00–16:00. There are also pickup points in front of the Wienglakor and Tip Chang hotels.

items.activity: Walk the Kad Kong Ta area and look at the old buildings on the old market road
items.note: Chinese-European shophouses line both sides of the street — the town's old trading quarter. You can admire the architecture even when it isn't a walking-market day.

items.activity: Stop by the Dhanabadee Ceramic Museum to learn where the chicken bowl comes from
items.note: There are demonstrations of shaping and hand-painting the traditional rooster design. The chicken bowl is a Lampang signature and now holds GI registration.

items.activity: Have lunch, then shop for souvenirs
items.note: Pick up chicken-bowl ceramics, with prices starting in the tens of baht, and some khao taen sugarcane crisps to take home.

items.activity: If you have time left, visit Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat Phra Chom Klao (Doi Phra Bat)
items.note: White chedis on a hilltop with a wide view, open roughly 06:00–17:00. A nice way to end the trip before heading home.

blocks.text: Adjusting the Plan to Your Time

items.name: Only 2 days, 1 night
items.blurb: Do Phrae quickly in half a day (Khum Chao Luang + Baan Wongburi), then drive over to sleep in Lampang. On day two, focus on the horse cart and Wat Phra That Lampang Luang.

items.name: Temple-and-merit focus
items.blurb: On the Phrae day, add Wat Phra That Cho Hae and Wat Chom Sawan; on the Lampang day, follow up with Wat Phra That Lampang Luang and Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat.

items.name: Traveling without a car
items.blurb: Take a bus or van between Phrae and Lampang, then use horse carts, songthaews, and motorbike taxis once you're in town. Staying near Kad Kong Ta is the most convenient.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The Lampang horse cart is a tourist activity, not high-speed transport. It moves slowly so you can soak up the atmosphere and take photos. Anyone expecting a thrill may find it underwhelming, but treated as an old-fashioned ride around town it's far more fun — and it helps the drivers earn a living and keep the trade alive.

faq.q: Is Phrae far from Lampang, and how long is the drive?
faq.a: Not far — about 64–70 km on Highway 103, then Phahonyothin Road, taking roughly 1 hour. The road is in good condition and easy going, so it works well to visit both provinces back to back in one trip.

faq.q: How much is a Lampang horse cart, and where do you catch one?
faq.a: The Lampang Horse Cart Association has three rates: 150 THB for a short loop, 200 THB for a longer loop, and 300 THB per hour to charter. The main pickup is the queue in front of the old provincial hall, running roughly 06:00–16:00. There are also pickup points in front of the Wienglakor and Tip Chang hotels.

faq.q: What are Wat Phra That Lampang Luang's hours, and where is it?
faq.a: Open daily 07:30–17:00. It's in Ko Kha district, about 18 km southwest of Lampang town — an easy stop while driving from Phrae into the city. The highlight is the upside-down reflection of the chedi cast inside a darkened hall.

faq.q: What's worth seeing in Phrae's old town?
faq.a: Mainly Khum Chao Luang Mueang Phrae (the teak mansion with 72 doors and windows), Baan Wongburi the century-old pink house (open 09:00–16:00, admission 30 THB), Baan Prataptjai or the Hundred-Pillar House, and Wat Phra That Cho Hae outside town, plus Baan Thung Hong, the home of mor hom cloth.

faq.q: Which day should I go to walk Kad Kong Ta?
faq.a: The Kad Kong Ta walking street opens only on Saturday and Sunday evenings, roughly 16:00–22:00. If you want to walk that market, line up your Saturday or Sunday night with the days you're in Lampang. The buildings in the Kad Kong Ta area, though, can be seen any day.
